paragraphs: Friend, here's what I take from Babel. These people had one language, one plan and a whole lot of brick. They said, "let us build for ourselves a city with a tower that reaches to the heavens, that we may make a name for ourselves and not be scattered over the face of all the earth" (Genesis 11:4). Notice how many times that sentence says "ourselves." I think the trouble was never the bricks. It was who the whole project was for.

And look at how it ended. They were building so they would NOT be scattered, and the LORD "scattered them from there over the face of all the earth" (Genesis 11:8). The very thing they planned to prevent is the thing that happened. I've been the stamper who thought he had to hold it all together by himself, and let me tell you, it is EXHAUSTING.

So here's your takeaway. A name worth having isn't one you build for yourself, it's one you receive from the God who made you. Next time you catch yourself stacking up bricks for your own name, whether it's at work, online or anywhere else, stop and hand the plans over to Him. He doesn't forget the small and the worn out, and He gives a better name than any tower can.
